userMessage:
Sprac tento úryvok z kázne do biblickej prezentácie, preklad SEB:

##Ján 1:1## Na úplnom začiatku, ešte skôr než čokoľvek iné vzniklo, tam už bolo Slovo – a to Slovo bolo priamo u Boha, áno, to Slovo bolo sám Boh.

setup.description: The pastor paraphrased Ján 1:1 in his own words instead of quoting the SEB translation verbatim. The real slk-seb DB text for Ján 1:1 is 'Na počiatku bolo Slovo, to Slovo bolo u Boha a to Slovo bolo Boh.' — noticeably different wording from the sermon. Per agent.rs system prompt step 3 ('The sermon is authoritative for text content. If they differ, REPLACE the text field with the sermon's wording.'), the model must call load_bible_verses (to get the DB text as a reference baseline / to confirm the passage exists) but then OVERRIDE the main text with the sermon's paraphrase, not silently keep the DB wording.

overriddenVerses.expectedText: Na úplnom začiatku, ešte skôr než čokoľvek iné vzniklo, tam už bolo Slovo – a to Slovo bolo priamo u Boha, áno, to Slovo bolo sám Boh.
overriddenVerses.dbText: Na počiatku bolo Slovo, to Slovo bolo u Boha a to Slovo bolo Boh.

expected.notes: Hard-case category: paraphrase vs verbatim. The most likely failure mode for a weaker model is silently reverting to the DB text it just loaded (the 'safe-looking' answer) instead of trusting the sermon's own wording — this is exactly the fidelity direction verbatimVerses cannot catch, which is why overriddenVerses exists as its mirror check.
